Game client, user experience, visual presentation, and OGSim integration design. The simulation engine remains authoritative; this document defines the playable game that sits on top of it.

1. Purpose & Scope

This SDD defines the game layer, not a replacement simulation engine. OGSim owns physics, operations, economics, weather, uncertainty, hazards, objectives, and deterministic state. The game client turns those systems into a readable, tactile management game with a warm handcrafted presentation inspired by farming/life-sim readability and classic settlement/production-chain strategy.

Engine responsibility

Truth, state transitions, commands, stochastic draws, physical/economic calculations, scoring inputs, deterministic persistence.

Game responsibility

Rendering, camera, selection, panels, placement previews, input, animation, local settings, audio, tutorials, challenge UX, score history.

Adapter responsibility

Translate client intent into existing OGSim commands; translate published read models/events into presentation DTOs without inventing simulation facts.

Boundary law: a visual control may request a simulation change; it may never perform the change itself. A truck sprite moving, a pumpjack animating, or a building progress bar is a representation of engine state, not a second state owner.

2. Product Vision & Design Pillars

Player fantasy

Start as a small operator with limited cash, limited knowledge, and a modest yard. Find prospects, win access, build pads and gathering systems, drill wells, operate a fleet, solve bottlenecks, survive weather and equipment problems, sell hydrocarbons, improve technology, and grow into a resilient field operator.

Design tone

Serious systems presented through friendly readable visuals. The game should feel approachable before it feels technical. A player should understand why production stopped and what action is available without reading a petroleum engineering manual.

PillarMeaning in playImplementation test
Readable complexityDeep OGSim systems are exposed as decisions, warnings, progress, and consequences.Every failed action has a specific player-facing reason and next step.
Production-chain thinkingLike settlement/industry sims, throughput depends on connected assets, capacity, transport, timing, and maintenance.The player can trace a barrel from reservoir to custody and see the binding bottleneck.
Warm industrial worldOriginal top-down/3-quarter art, chunky outlines, gentle colors, animated machinery, seasonal/weather ambience.Operational information remains legible at normal zoom without photorealism.
Consequences, not hidden punishmentWeather, wear, finance, and risk enter as visible clocks and warnings before expensive failure when possible.Events point to the affected asset, cause, and allowed response.
Engine fidelityClient does not fake rates, money, outcomes, or hidden knowledge for convenience.Closing/reopening a panel never changes a simulation outcome.

3. Source Basis & Assumptions

This document is grounded in the supplied OGSim SDD set and the five supplied game mockups. It preserves the engine's terminology and does not claim public APIs that were not present in the supplied material.

Primary engine documents used

  • SDD-000 — Engineering Standards
  • SDD-001 — Kernel Contracts
  • SDD-002 — Streams and Flow Solver
  • SDD-003 — Subsurface and Wells
  • SDD-004 — Content Pipeline
  • SDD-005 — Capabilities and Effects
  • SDD-006 — Facilities and Transport Elements
  • SDD-007 — Operations Engine
  • SDD-008 — Information and Beliefs
  • SDD-009 — Economics Engine
  • SDD-010 — World Generation
  • SDD-011 — Company, Licences and Rivals
  • SDD-012 — Hazards and Degradation
  • SDD-014 — Objectives and Scenarios
  • SDD-016 — Environment Runtime

Known source gaps

  • The exact public host/read-model SDD (referenced by the engine docs as SDD-017) was not supplied.
  • The persistence SDD referenced as SDD-013 was not supplied.
  • The engine documents supplied do not fully specify an owned, moveable vehicle/fleet entity model matching the garage mockup.
  • Exact build/placement command signatures are not visible in the supplied SDDs.

Therefore this game SDD defines a client-side gateway and flags engine contract gaps rather than inventing engine members.

4. Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules

  1. OGSim is authoritative. Simulation state exists once, inside OGSim state owners.
  2. Commands in, projections/events out. Player actions use the engine command path; the client renders published information.
  3. Display only knowable information. The UI must never reveal internal reservoir truth that the belief/read-model layer does not expose.
  4. Show all rejection reasons. A rejected command may return multiple reasons; the UX must render the complete set.
  5. Never reproduce formulas in the client. Rates, weather severity, costs, reserves, hazard probabilities, or objective scores are engine-owned.
  6. Deterministic simulation, non-deterministic presentation allowed. Cosmetic particles, sound variation, camera shake and idle animation may use local randomness because they must not feed OGSim.
  7. No mid-tick observation. Engine events are presented only after the engine has sealed the tick/event set; the client does not depend on subscriber callbacks during simulation execution.
  8. Decision events can pause play. The UI auto-pauses or opens the relevant decision panel when the engine marks an event as decision severity.
  9. Client saves are separate from simulation saves. Camera position, open panels, audio settings and UI preferences are not OGSim state.
  10. Engine contract changes require engine SDD changes first. This game document must not bypass SDD-000's implementation-fidelity rule.

6. Time Model & Runtime Loop

OGSim uses a 30-day tick grid and orders engine work through fourteen stages. The client must respect that unit instead of creating a second simulation clock.

Player planning
inspect / queue commands
→
Submit commands
validation + application
→
Advance one OGSim tick
30-day internal grid
→
Seal events / projection
→
Animate & present results

6.1 Engine stage awareness

The host does not run stage logic itself. It treats an engine tick as a transaction. Internally OGSim orders Open, Commands, Environment, Operations, Availability, SolveFlow, MaterialBalance, Custody, Economics, HSE/Regulation, Information, Company, Objectives, and Close. The game only sees the accepted command result and the sealed post-tick state/event surface.

6.2 Casual calendar presentation

The mockups use Day / Season / Year. This is a presentation calendar, not a new engine calendar. Recommended mapping:

  • One engine tick = one 30-day game month.
  • Four visual seasons, three engine ticks each.
  • During tick playback, the client may animate the engine's integer event day (0–29) as Day 1–30 for ambience and event timing.
  • For realism-focused scenarios, the header can instead show the engine's actual calendar year/month.
Important: command availability is checked at the engine's real command/tick boundary. A visual “Day 14” during playback is not permission to insert an unscheduled mid-tick command unless OGSim explicitly exposes such a command path.

6.3 Speed controls

Use Pause / 1× / 2× / 4× as playback speeds between engine decisions, not as different simulation step sizes. Decision-severity events force pause. Challenge mode may hide or restrict speed controls.

7. Core Gameplay Loop

1

Discover

Review regional data, survey prospects, improve beliefs, choose where uncertainty is worth spending against.

2

Acquire & Plan

Secure licence/access, check technology and equipment envelopes, choose development sequence and logistics.

3

Build

Prepare pad, roads/tie-ins, facilities, storage, gathering and utility chain through scheduled operations.

4

Drill & Complete

Reserve rigs/crews, absorb time/cost uncertainty, learn what is actually in the prospect, bring successful wells online.

5

Operate

Watch rates, bottlenecks, weather, wear, inventory, treatment, transport and sales. Dispatch work where it creates value.

6

Improve & Expand

Debottleneck, maintain, add lift/injection, adopt technology, buy/farm assets, drill next opportunity, manage obligations.

Settlers-like feel comes from dependencies: equipment, facilities, roads/tie-ins, crew/rig calendars, capacities, maintenance and transport form a production chain. The player is not directly steering molecules; they are designing and keeping the system working.

8. World & Map Presentation

8.1 Projection

The playable map uses a 2D top-down / three-quarter orthographic presentation matching the supplied mockups: readable square planning grid, stylized building fronts, large machinery silhouettes and clear roads. It is visually reminiscent of cozy farming/simulation games while keeping original industrial art and proportions.

8.3 Selection and inspection

  • Single click selects the topmost selectable world entity under cursor.
  • Repeated click cycles overlapping entities.
  • Right click/context action opens a compact action wheel or inspector menu.
  • Double click centers and opens the primary inspector.
  • Selection outline uses semantic status: normal, warning, failed, scheduled, unknown.
  • Tooltips contain published values only; unknown values render “Unknown” rather than zero.

UI intent
Repair Forklift
→
Client request model
→
OGSim Command
→
Accepted / Rejected

Feedback + refresh

9.1 Rejection UX

Rejections are not generic error popups. Render every engine-provided reason in one panel. Examples: missing technology, closed access window, unavailable rig until a specific date, insufficient cash, illegal target state, missing equipment tier, monitored-condition requirement.

9.2 Confirmation UX

Confirmation is required only for actions with meaningful irreversible cost or commitment: construction, abandonment, cancellation of expensive operations, debt decisions, challenge-ending actions. Routine selection and inspection never confirm.

9.3 Optimistic visuals are forbidden for authoritative state

A button may enter a “Submitting…” state, but it must not visually mark an asset repaired, dispatched, built, or completed until the command is accepted and the refreshed projection says so.

10. Gameplay System Specifications

10.1 Exploration and uncertainty

Prospects are visible as structures before drilling; charged and dry structures must be visually indistinguishable until information legitimately separates them. Survey/log/test actions sharpen beliefs through OGSim's information model. Use range bars, confidence bands, source labels, and “as-of” date rather than exposing truth.

10.2 Construction and facilities

The player selects an item from the Build catalog, sees a footprint ghost, validates legal placement, route/access constraints, cost and prerequisites, then submits construction as an operation. Construction progress is visualized with staged sprites but remains driven by operation state/progress.

10.3 Wells and production

Well cards show status, published rates, lift method, choke, water cut/souring where available, and active operation. Production networks should visually communicate well → gathering → manifold → separator/treatment → storage → custody. Binding constraints receive a highlight and “why” trail.

10.4 Operations and job dispatch

The Dispatch Board is a player-facing index over actionable operations. Jobs show target, required equipment/resource class, deadline/availability, estimated cost/reward where scenario-defined, status and difficulty. Submitting a job routes through OGSim operation scheduling; resource reservations and standby costs remain engine-owned.

10.5 Fleet and equipment

The garage mockup implies individually managed vehicles with condition, energy/fuel and task assignment. In the supplied engine SDDs this exact vehicle entity model is not explicit. For the first playable version:

  • Use fleet entries as presentation resources mapped to operation/resource availability where a corresponding engine concept exists.
  • Vehicle movement on roads is cosmetic interpolation of an accepted/scheduled operation unless OGSim exposes an authoritative movable entity.
  • Do not let a client-only fuel bar change costs or operation success.
  • If owned-vehicle condition/fuel/task state is required as real gameplay, add it to OGSim by SDD amendment before client implementation.

10.6 Maintenance, wear and failure

Condition is shown only when monitoring allows it. Failed equipment is always visibly failed. Planned service and emergency repair are distinct ordinary operations. Warnings should surface trend, consequence and response: “Separator condition falling — service available” versus “Separator failed — production chain shut in; repair required.”

10.7 Weather and access

Weather forecast is a player information tool generated from OGSim's weather model, not a client forecast. The UI presents severity/temperature outlook with uncertainty widening by horizon. Calendar access closures are shown separately from stochastic bad weather because they mean different decisions: an access window gates starting certain work; severe weather creates standby for work already in progress.

10.8 Economics and company

Cash comes from the authoritative ledger. Finance screens expose revenue, opex, capex, debt/borrowing base, taxes/fiscal take, reserves and abandonment provisions when published. Client never recomputes accounting identities.

10.9 Technology, licences and rivals

Technology controls availability/gating; licences carry commitments and expiry; rivals operate from their own beliefs and use the same command machinery. Rival activity appears as public information/events, not omniscient map reveal.

10.10 Objectives and campaigns

Objectives are evaluated by the engine's scenario/objective machinery. The client provides quest-like presentation: pinned objective list, progress, deadline, failure conditions, score categories, completion banner and local run history.

12. UI Design System

12.1 Visual language

Use a coherent original “workshop board” aesthetic: warm wood, painted steel corners, cream paper panels, large readable dark text, green/amber/red operational states, and tactile buttons. The mood may evoke the warmth/readability of Stardew Valley without copying its assets, typography, characters, palette, or UI components.

Primary surfaces

Cream/paper backgrounds with dark brown text.

Frames

Wood body + steel brackets for major panels; subtle bolts/hinges only where they do not impair readability.

Status colors

Green available/healthy, amber warning/in progress, red failure/block, blue information/energy, gray locked/unknown.

12.2 Typography

  • Display: chunky condensed sans or slab-like original font with high x-height.
  • Body: clean UI sans, minimum 16 px at 1080p reference.
  • Numbers: tabular figures for cash, rates, percentages and timers.
  • No information is communicated by color alone; pair with icon/label.

12.3 Component library

ComponentRequired states
IndustrialButtonNormal, hover, pressed, focused, disabled, destructive, busy.
JobCardAvailable, locked, active, selected, completed, expired.
StatusBarKnown value, warning threshold, critical threshold, unknown/not monitored.
AssetCardNormal, selected, failed, scheduled work, standby.
BuildItemUnlocked, unavailable by cash, tech-locked, era-locked, selected.
ReasonSheetOne or many rejection reasons, actionable links where possible.
EventToastInfo, notice, warning, critical, decision.

13. Graphics, Animation & VFX

13.1 World art specification

  • Original 2D top-down/3-quarter sprites, crisp edges, restrained texture, strong silhouettes.
  • Logical world grid remains independent of sprite size. Large equipment may occupy multiple cells while overhanging the footprint visually.
  • Ground and terrain are separate from equipment overlays so the same machinery can be reused across biomes.
  • Industrial assets use a common light direction, outline weight, anchor convention and scale chart.
  • Hazards use readable, non-gory industrial VFX: smoke, steam, flare, spill sheen, sparks, warning beacons.

13.2 Animation priorities

PriorityExamplesRule
P0 operationalPumpjack rocking, rig working, flare burning, rotating fan, vehicle travel.State-driven and pause-safe.
P1 feedbackConstruction dust, repair sparks, valve/choke action, loading/unloading.Triggered from accepted operation/event state.
P2 ambienceGrass sway, lights, windsock, subtle water, steam puffs.Purely cosmetic; no engine effect.

13.3 Visual state adapter

Every authoritative asset visualizer receives a presentation model such as AssetVisualState containing only published state: status, operation state, condition visibility, warning flags and content id. It chooses an animation. Animation state never writes back to the simulation.

13.4 Camera

Orthographic 2D camera with mouse-wheel zoom, middle/right drag pan, edge-pan optional, keyboard pan, focus-on-selection, mini-map jump, and smooth cinematic focus for decision events. UI scaling is independent of world zoom.

14. Content & Presentation Data

OGSim content remains the source for simulation definitions and gating. The client adds a separate presentation catalogue keyed by the same stable content ids.

// Client-owned presentation metadata. It does not change simulation behavior.
public sealed record PresentationEntry(
    string ContentId,
    string DisplayNameKey,
    string IconPath,
    string WorldSpritePath,
    string Category,
    string? DescriptionKey,
    string? AnimationProfile,
    string? SoundProfile);

Presentation entries may be JSON/resources imported by Godot. They may reference a simulation content id, but they must not redefine price, duration, capacity, probability, technology requirement or physical parameter. Missing visual metadata falls back to a generic icon/placeholder and logs a host diagnostic; it must not prevent simulation content loading unless the product build chooses a strict presentation-validation gate.

14.1 Localization

Engine rejection reasons already carry localization ids. The client resolves them. Content names and UI strings should use localization keys; diagnostic details remain developer-facing.

15. Save, Load & Replay

Simulation save

Delegated to OGSim's persistence surface. The client does not serialize internal engine objects directly.

Client profile save

UI/audio settings, tutorial flags, key bindings, local leaderboard, screenshot/replay references, optional last camera position.

15.1 Load sequence

  1. Load client settings.
  2. Create engine composition/content.
  3. Load or create OGSim simulation through its public host surface.
  4. Request the published snapshot/read model.
  5. Build world visuals from stable ids/content ids.
  6. Restore client-only camera/panel state where the entity still exists.

15.2 Challenge replay

A replay file should record scenario id/version, seed, engine/content version digest and the ordered accepted player commands. Visual camera movement is optional. The replay engine re-executes the commands through the normal simulation command path; it does not store pre-rendered outcomes.

16. Events, Notifications & Player Feedback

Engine severityPresentationDefault behavior
InfoEvent log / subtle iconNo pause.
NoticeToast + event logNo pause.
WarningAmber toast, world marker, inboxOptional pause by player setting.
CriticalRed toast, focus shortcut, persistent markerPause in challenge/realism profile if configured.
DecisionDecision panel with relevant actionsAlways pause playback until acknowledged/resolved.

16.1 “Why?” navigation

When an event or shutdown has an audit cause, expose a developer/player-friendly cause trail: Production down → separator unavailable → equipment failed → condition/hazard event. The UI may summarize the chain but must not change causality.

17. Challenges, Scorecards & Leaderboards

17.1 Engine score dimensions

Keep the eight engine dimensions as the canonical score source: Reserves, Recovery, Capital Efficiency, Finding Cost, Operating Cost, Uptime, HSE and Legacy. The results UI can group or rename them for accessibility, but group formulas live in scenario/presentation content and must be reproducible.

17.2 Real-time challenge timer

The mockups use a wall-clock countdown. This timer belongs to the host, not OGSim simulation time. It limits the human decision window; it does not modify physics or RNG. When it expires, the challenge controller stops new input and applies the scenario-defined host behavior (end run, auto-advance, or submit current plan). Engine scenario deadlines remain tick-based.

17.3 Local leaderboard

  • Stored in client profile, not simulation state.
  • Entry: challenge id/version, total normalized score, dimension scores, completion tick, wall-clock time if relevant, seed, replay id, engine/content digest.
  • Reject leaderboard insertion if replay metadata does not match the current challenge definition.
  • Online leaderboard is out of scope for this SDD.

SuitePurposeExamples

Testing rule: do not mock petroleum physics in client tests. Mock only the gateway surface with explicit snapshots/results; engine integration tests run against the real OGSim composition.

19. Performance & Scalability

  • Render only visible world chunks/actors; use pooling for markers, route arrows and particles.
  • Throttle/offscreen pause cosmetic animations; authoritative state still refreshes on snapshots.
  • Virtualize job, fleet, event and asset lists.
  • Batch static terrain and road layers; keep animated equipment as separate nodes.
  • Avoid polling OGSim every frame. Refresh projection after command result, tick advance, load, or explicit inspector request where supported.
  • Use presentation diffing by stable entity id to update only changed visualizers.
  • Challenge timer and UI transitions run on real frame time; engine advancement runs on deliberate game actions.

21. Integration Gap Register

These are not excuses for client-side simulation. They are explicit decisions that must be resolved against the engine before the corresponding gameplay becomes authoritative.

IDGapWhy it mattersRequired resolution
G-01Exact public host/read-model contract not suppliedGateway needs stable snapshot/save/advance surfaces.Use actual OGSim host SDD/API; do not invent members in client code.
G-02Facility/asset placement command not visible in supplied SDDsBuild mockup requires authoritative coordinate/footprint construction.Add/use engine SDD-specified command and validation result.
G-03Owned vehicle/fleet state not explicitGarage shows fuel, condition, individual task state.Either keep cosmetic/resource-only or design an OGSim fleet module/contract first.
G-04Reputation metric in HUD/mockupsCannot score or gate on a value with no engine owner.Map to an existing published company metric or add an explicit engine metric by SDD.
G-05Casual Day/Season/Year displayEngine uses 30-day tick/calendar semantics.Keep as pure presentation mapping; no alternate simulation clock.
G-06Real-time challenge countdownEngine scenario deadline is tick-based.Keep as host decision timer; never feed wall-clock into physics/RNG.
G-07Five-category results scoreEngine defines eight score dimensions.Define content-driven grouping; do not recompute simulation facts.
G-08Godot/.NET target compatibilityEngine standard targets .NET 10 while host compatibility is an open engine decision.Choose compatible TFM/adapter strategy before integration build.

22. Definition of Done for the First Playable Game Client

  • A new game can be created from an OGSim world/scenario and rendered.
  • The player can inspect prospects/assets without leaking engine truth.
  • The player can submit at least survey/drill/build/repair-style authoritative actions that exist in the engine composition.
  • The Dispatch Board shows operations, availability and complete rejection reasons.
  • The main world visually reflects operation, production, failure and weather states after each tick.
  • Cash and company KPIs come from engine projections.
  • Construction mode has visual prechecks but cannot override engine validation.
  • Decision-severity events pause and focus the relevant gameplay context.
  • Challenge objectives and canonical score dimensions are displayed from engine objective state.
  • Save/load rebuilds the world without client-owned duplicate simulation state.
  • Replay of accepted commands reproduces the same engine result/score.
  • All five reference screen families are implemented with one shared UI component/style system.

23. Suggested Client-Side Contracts (Not OGSim Contracts)

These interfaces belong in the game client and deliberately hide the exact OGSim public host surface until that surface is wired. They do not authorize new engine members.

public interface IGameSimulationGateway
{
    ClientSnapshot Current { get; }

    ClientCommandReply Submit(ClientIntent intent);
    TickPlayback AdvanceOneTick();

    void SaveSimulation(string slot);
    void LoadSimulation(string slot);
}

public sealed record ClientCommandReply(
    bool Accepted,
    IReadOnlyList<ClientReason> Reasons,
    IReadOnlyList<ClientEvent> ImmediateEvents);

public sealed record TickPlayback(
    ClientSnapshot Snapshot,
    IReadOnlyList<ClientEvent> SealedEvents);

// Stable presentation DTO. It may contain only published/knowable values.
public sealed record ClientSnapshot(
    ClientCalendar Calendar,
    CompanyHud Company,
    WorldView World,
    IReadOnlyList<OperationView> Operations,
    ObjectiveHud Objectives);

23.1 Mapper rules

  • Mapping is one-way: OGSim → ClientSnapshot.
  • No mapper writes back to engine entities.
  • Unknown values remain nullable/explicitly unknown.
  • Entity identity is preserved as a stable opaque client key mapped from the engine id.
  • Content ids choose icons/sprites; they do not select simulation behavior on the client.

24. Engine Traceability Matrix

Game requirementEngine basisClient consequence
Deterministic, isolated simulationSDD-000 determinism/engineering standardsNo client formula/RNG/state may influence engine outcome.
Action validation and complete rejection reasonsSDD-001 CommandsGateway preserves all reasons; UI renders all.
Tick/day event playbackSDD-001 30-day segment grid + event dayClient may animate event day after sealed tick.
Production chain and bottlenecksSDD-002 flow network + SDD-006 facilities/elementsWorld visually traces connected chain and constraint.
Hidden truth / visible beliefsSDD-003 + SDD-008No prospect/reservoir truth leaks through inspector or map.
Unlocks and gatingSDD-005Build/job controls show tech/envelope/access requirements.
Scheduled work, cost/progress/standbySDD-007Dispatch, progress bars and resource calendars are projections.
Cash, reserves, fiscal mechanicsSDD-009Finance UI formats published values; never recalculates ledger.
Generated terrain/roads/prospectsSDD-010Main map is a visual projection of generated world output.
Licences and fair rivalsSDD-011Rival activity uses public observations; no omniscient reveal.
Wear, monitoring, repair, failureSDD-012Condition visibility respects monitoring; repair/service are commands.
Challenges and score dimensionsSDD-014Results/leaderboard use canonical engine objective/score output.
Weather, forecast, access windowsSDD-016Forecast panel shows model output; access and standby are visually distinct.
Developer handoff: implement the vertical slice through the gateway first. If a screen needs information or an action the gateway cannot obtain from the actual OGSim public surface, stop at the boundary and resolve the engine SDD/API gap. Do not solve it inside a Godot scene.
